Interesting! The tarball downloads are actually fast (2.2 MB/s, 1.4 MB/s) — the slow part is the **metadata** requests (packument lookups), which were taking 10–50 seconds. pnpm's `minimumReleaseAge` check needs full metadata (the packument containing the `time` field), and those requests are timing out.

So the real problem is: the registry metadata endpoint (`https://registry.npmjs.org/<pkg>`) is slow/unstable (10–20 seconds per request), and pnpm's `fetchTimeout: 1e5` (100 seconds) should be sufficient… but the earlier failure was "operation was aborted due to timeout." The install was run in a background process via `just up`, which inherited stdio — it's possible that pnpm's fetch retries gave up on some requests after several minutes.

Wait, but there's something I still haven't been able to figure out: where does `minimumReleaseAge` come from? It's not in the repository configuration, and `pnpm config get minimumReleaseAge` shows undefined. But the error message said "7 lockfile entries failed verification: @firebase/auth-types@0.13.2 could not be checked against minimumReleaseAge (operation was aborted due to timeout)."

Hmm — let me re-read the earlier error:

```
[ERR_PNPM_MINIMUM_RELEASE_AGE_VIOLATION] 7 lockfile entries failed verification:
  @firebase/auth-types@0.13.2 could not be checked against minimumReleaseAge (The operation was aborted due to timeout)
```

So this check is definitely enabled. And "could not be checked" — meaning it couldn't verify (because of the timeout), and since it can't confirm the package is old enough, it treats it as a violation. So `minimumReleaseAge` is set somewhere. Let me check the pnpm 11 defaults… maybe in pnpm 11 it's enabled by default at some value? Or maybe the repo is configuring it via pnpm-workspace.yaml under a `pnpm:` key? Let me look at the whole pnpm-workspace.yaml once more — the top-level keys I saw were: packages, allowBuilds, catalog, onlyBuiltDependencies, overrides. There's no minimumReleaseAge.
